caseno: Appeal from Original Decree No. 20 of 1983 with Civil Rule No. 158 (C) of 1982.
lawyer:
M Fazlul Karim ----- For the Appellant. 
AKM Shafiqur Rahman with Shahabuddin Faiz and Mustafa Kamal Pasha ----- For the Respondent.
parties:
MM Zaman ----- Appellant
Vs.
Sakina Ahmed  ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
FHM Habibur Rahman J: This appeal is directed against the judgment and decree passed by Mr Jalaluddin Ahmed, Sub-ordinate Judge, 1st Court Chittagong on 21-8-82 in other Suit No. 37/79 decreeing the suit for ejectment of the monthly tenant and for recovery of the arrear rent. 

 2. Plaintiff respondent Mrs. Sakina Ahmed instituted the present suit on 20-3-79 contending, inter alia, as follows-The suit premises in question is a three storied building named "Surma House" at 16 Joynagar, Mohalla Chowkbazar, Chittagong Municipal Area. The plaintiff Mrs. Sakina Ahmed purchased the suit property from the previous owner Mrs. Zebunnessa Kabir by registered kabala dated 6-5-74. The defendant M.M. Zaman was a temporary monthly tenant under plaintiff's vendor Mrs, Zebunnessa Kabir in respect of the 2nd floor of the three storied building on a monthly rent of Taka 600 payable according to the English calendar month. The plaintiff's vendor Mrs. Zebunnessa Kabir wrote a letter of adornment dated 10-5-74 to the defendant tenant informing him about the sale and asking him to attorn the plaintiff as landlord and pay rent to the plaintiff with effect from 1st May 1974. The plaintiff after purchase thoroughly renovated the house providing for better amenities to the tenant. The monthly rent continued to be Taka 600 per month upto 31st December, 1974. There was an oral agreement on 1-1-75 between the plaintiff through her son in law PW 1. Hossain Iman Chowdhury and according to that agreement defendant promised to pay an enhanced rent to Taka 1000 only per month with effect from 1-1-75. The defendant paid rent for some months at the rate of Taka 1000 only per month but subsequently being ill-advised the defendant wanted to avoid payment of rent and made several applications to the different authorities even questioning the title of the plaintiff but in vain. Apprehending repetition of such kinds of harassment the plaintiff wanted a written agreement. Accordingly a written agreement was signed and executed by the plaintiff and the defendant on 1-7-76 incorporating the stipulation that the defendant would pay a rent to of Taka 1,000 per month for the said premises to the plaintiff. The defendant wrote letters to the plaintiff admitting the rate of rent with effect from 1-1-75 to be Taka 1000 per month. On 22-10-76 the defendant wrote to the husband of the plaintiff admitting the rate of rent to be Taka 1000 per month with effect from 1-1-75 admitting the arrear rent from 1-1-75 to 30-6-76 and solicited a remission of Taka 1800 out of a total arrear of rent of Taka 18000 on the ground of slump in his business. On the same day the defendant wrote another letter wrongly showing the arrear rent Taka 900 per month with effect from 1-1-75 instead of Taka 1000 per month apparently soliciting remission of rent by Taka 100 per month for 18 months from 1-1-75 to 30-6-76 on the alleged ground of slump in business. The defendant did not pay the rent month to month. The defendant is a habitual defaulter. After repeated demands he used to remit some rent. As the rent was fixed at Taka 1000 per month with effect from 1-1-75 the present case does not come within the mischief of Martial Law Regulation No. 11 of 1976 dated 8-1-76; but the defendants started avoiding payment of rent on the plea of the said Martial Law Regulation. The defendant caused serious damages to the suit premises by making garden and depositing earth on the top floor of the suit premises. From May 1974 to December 1974 Taka 4800 was the arrear rent @ Taka 600 for eight months. From 1st January 1975 to 31st March 1978 for 19 months the arrear rent was Taka 39,000 at the rate of Taka 1000 per month. Upto 31st March 1978 the defendant paid in total a sum of Taka 28200. Therefore, the plaintiff was still a defaulter in respect of payment of rent for an amount of Taka 16500. The plaintiff finding no other alternative terminated the tenancy of the defendant with the expiry of 31st March 1978 by sending a notice through her Advocate on 20-1-78 by registered post which was duty served on the defendant who gave an evasive reply to the said notice. The defendant did not pay the arrear rent and compensation for unauthorized occupation with effect from 1-4-78 at the rate of Taka 40 per day as demanded by the plaintiff. The plaintiff was therefore, constrained to file the present suit on 20-3-79 for ejectment, recovery of arrear rent of Taka 15600 and compensation of Taka 14000 for 350 days since the expiry of 31-3-78 @ Taka 40 per day for unauthorized occupation. 

 3. The defendant contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the material allegations. The defendant contended that the suit is barred under the principles of waiver, acquiescence and estoppels. The plaintiff did not renovate the suit premises after purchase and did not provide for better amenities. There was no oral agreement on 1-1-75 between the plaintiff and the defendant through her son in law and the defendant never promised to pay Taka 1000 as rent with effect from 1-1-75. The defendant never paid rent at the rate of Taka. 1000 with effect from 1-1-75. The defendant is a bonafide tenant in the suit premises since 1967 at a rent of Taka 600 per month by regularly paying rent to the previous owner Mrs. Zebunnessa Kabir. In May 1974 Mrs. Zebunnessa Kabir informed the defendant regarding the transfer of the suit premises to the plaintiff. The defendant accordingly sent letter to her village home address (village Daulatpur, PS Fatickchari, Chittagong) which was given by the previous owner in her letter of Attornment of May, 1974 to the defendant. And in the said letter defendant requested the plaintiff to send a representative to collect the rent but the letter came back with the remark "addressee not found". As the such the defendant was unable to pay rent to anyone. In the meantime the defendant came to know from the occupant of the 1st floor of the suit premises that the house in question was recorded as non-resident property. So the defendant wrote to the Assistant Controller (Exchange Control Department), Bangladesh Bank, Chittagong 18-1-75 and was intimated that the scheduled premises belonged to a non-resident that the rent should be paid to the non-resident account and that the defendant was also informed that further decision in the matter would be communicated to him latter. Because of this letter of the Exchange Control Department of the Bangladesh Bank, Chittagong the defendant for some time could not pay rent to anybody. On 22-5-75 the Exchange Control Department of Bangladesh Bank, Dhaka wrote to this defendant asking for certain information which was replied to by the defendant by this letter dated 2-6-75. Thereafter, the Exchange Control Department of Bangladesh Bank, Dhaka wrote a letter on 1-7-76 to the defendant informing that they had no objection in the matter of payment of the rent to the plaintiff by the defendant on 1-7-76 by exercising undue influence an agreement of lease was executed between the defendant and the plaintiff providing for payment of Taka 1000 per month. This agreement was effected by the plaintiff by misrepresentation and fraud and by suppressing the fact of promulgation of Martial Law Regulation No. 11 of 1976. The defendant in the meantime came to know of the Martial Law Regulation No. 11 of 1976 wherein it was provided that where the rent of any premises was not more than one thousand Taka per month on 1-12-75 it shall not be increased. Therefore, the agreement between the plaintiff and defendant dated 1-7-76 is of no effect and the rent by operation of Martial Law Regulation No. 11 of 1976 continued to be Taka 600 per month. On 21-10-76 the defendant was called to the residence of PW 1 Mr. Hossain Imam Chowdhury, son-in-law and legal representative of the plaintiff at Enayet Bazar where the defendant was compelled to write a letter under duress at the insistence of the said Mr. Hossain Imam Chowdhury providing for enhanced rent of Taka 900 per month with effect from January 1976. The contents of that letter so far as it relates to enhancement of rent having been obtained by fraud and coercion under duress after promulgation of the aforesaid Martial law Regulation No. 11 of 1976 is pull and void. The plaintiff has been demanding rent at the enhanced rate of Taka 1000 per month and the defdt. According to law being entitled to pay Taka 600 per month has been trying to pay the said amount to the plaintiff but the plaintiff did not accept the amount and has been illegally demanding increased rent contrary to law. Under the aforesaid circumstance the defendant paid rents in lump at the rate of Taka 600 per month to the plaintiff till March 1978 through her son in law and local representative and through postal money orders and the plaintiff accepted the amount without any objection. The plaintiff refused and did not accept the rent of the month of April 1978 sent through money order No. 2327 date 9-5-78 and the money order was returned to the defendant with postal remarks "refused". Hence the defendant had no other alternative but to deposit the same in court of the House Rent Controller u/s 19 of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance and started to deposit the monthly rent there and has been continuing to deposit the same. 

 4. On behalf of the plaintiff landlady, her son in law Md. Hossain Imam Chowdhury who resides in Chittagong and looks after all matters relating to plaintiffs leased out premises in question was examined as PW 1. Exhibit it is agreement dated 1-7-76 between the plaintiff and the defendant. Exhibits 2(a) and 2 are both letters dated 22-7-76 written by defdt. Respectively to the plaintiff and her husband Mr. Bazal Ahmed, General Manager Janata Bank, Dhaka. The plaintiff and her husband reside at 542, Dhanmondi R/A, Road No. 12 Dhaka Exhibit 2 is addressed to Mr. Bazal Ahmed, Exhibit 2 shows arrear rent from January, 1975 to June 1976 at the rate of Taka 900 per month addressed to the plaintiff, which is explained in the letter Exhibit 2 (a) soliciting remission of rent of Taka 1800 for eighteen months from 1-1-75 to 30-6-76 Taka 100 less rent per month for the said period of eighteen months. Exhibit 3 is notice dated 20-8-78 u/s 106 of the Transfer of property Act sent by the plaintiffs Advocate to the defdt. Exhibit 4 (lump are two postal receipts date. 20-1-78 showing sending of plaintiffs notices u/s 106 TP Act to defdt's business address and another to the defdt's residential address. Exhibit 5 is defdt's reply dated 18-3-78 to plaintiffs notice date. 20-1-78 u/s 106 of the Transfer of Property Act. On behalf of the defdt DW 1 MM Zaman (Defdt. Himself) and DW 2 Abdul Hai (an employee of Bangladesh Bank Ctg) were examined DW 2 proved nothing Exhibit A is the previous owner's letter of attainment date 10-5-74 addressed to the deft Exhibit A (1) is the letter date 1st July, 1976 addressed to the deft by the Controller of Foreign Exchange, Dhaka asking the defdt to pay rent to the plaintiff soon. Exhibit A (2) is the letter date 19-10-77 of the plaintiff to the defdt asking the defdt to pay arrear rent of Taka 20,800 to the plaintiff's representative and son-in-law Mr Hossain Chowdhury, 2 Enayet Bazar, Ctg (Telephone No. 80202) and asking the defdt to vacate the premises by 31-10-77 Exhibit A (3) in the letter dated 24-6-74 written by defdt to the plaintiff at her village address (village Daulatpur, PS Fatikchari Dist Chittagong) which came back to the defdt, unserved Exhibit A (4) is office copy of the letter Exhibit A (3) Exhibit B to Exhibit B (14) are 15 money order receipts showing sending of a total amount of Taka 16,600 in lump as arrear rents sent between 13-10-77 to 18-10-77 be defdt to plaintiff Exhibit B(15) to Exhibit B (18) are 4 money order receipts showing sending of a total amount of Taka 2400 at the rate of Taka 600 per month by defdt to the plaintiff between 3-11-77 to 9-3-78 Exhibit C is a receipt of rent of Taka 600 for the month of February, 1974 granted by previous owner Zebunnessa Kabir on 17-4-74 in favour of defdt Exhibit D is the envelop of regd letter sent by defdt to plaintiff's address showing return to defdt with the remark 'not found" in June, 1974, Exhibit E is the postal receipt dated 25-6-74 of the letter Exhibit A (3) dated 24-6-74 is envelope Exhibit D Exhibit F is the acknowledgment due receipt of letter Exhibit A (4) returned unserved Exhibit A (5) is the alleged office copy of defdt's letter dated 18-1-75 addressed to the Asst. Controller, Exchange Control Deptt, Ctg Exhibit A(6) is an alleged letter Date 22-1-75 of Asstt. Controller of Bangladesh Bank, Exchange Control Deptt, Ctg written in pencil not duly proved Exhibit A(7) is a letter dated 22-5-75 from Exchange Control Deptt of Bangladesh Bank to the deft Exhibit A(8) is an office copy of deft's letter dated 2-6-75 sent to the Exchange Control Office Bangladesh Bank, Dhaka Exhibit A (9) is a letter date 10-10-77 by the deft to the plaintiff admitting a total arrear of rent of Taka 11600 even at the monthly rate of Taka 600/- which alone abundantly proves that the deft is a habitual defaulter from May 1974 to September 1977 and in this letter Exhibit A(9) the defdt took the plea of Martial Law Regulation II of 1976 prohibiting enhancement of rent which is not more than Taka 1000 per month on 1-12-75 and by the said letter Exhibit A(9) Date 10-10-77 defdt, only promised to pay the arrear rent soon. Exhibit-G is the challan dated 30-5-78 depositing rent of Taka 600 for the premises in question by the deft. In favour of the plaintiff in the House Rent Control Case No. 208 of 1978, Exhibit G(1) Exhibit G(5) are challans showing deposit of rents at the rate of Taka 600 per month from May 1978 to June 1982. 

 5. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge decreed the suit in favour to the plaintiff finding that admittedly the defendant was a tenant in respect of the suit premises under the previous owner Mrs Zebunnessa Kabir, the defdt continued to be a tenant under the plaintiff who purchased the suit premises from the previous owner as proved by defendant's letter Exhibit A 3 dated 24-6-74 addressed to the plaintiff, that the defdt, paid rent to the plff. at the rate of Taka 600 from May 1974 to December 1974, that it has been proved from defdt's letter Exhibit 2 and 2(a) as well as from the evidence of PW 1 Md Hossain Imam Chowdhury that by oral agreement the defdt agreed to pay rent of Taka 1000 per month with effect from 1st January, 1975 to the plff. in respect of the suit premises, that the trial court disbelieved the defdt's story the Exhibit 2 and 2(a) were obtained by Pw 1 (son-in-law of the plff) from the defdt. by duress or threat or coercion, that it has been amply proved that the rent of the suit premises was agreed to be paid by the defdt at the rate of Taka 1,000 with effect from 1st January, 1975, that it has also been proved sufficiently that the defdt, habitually defaulted in payment of rent and is therefore, a defaulter, that the tenancy has been validly terminated by the plff. with effect from 31st March 1978 by duly serving notice u/s 106 of the Transfer of Property Act on the defdt, that the rent due from 1st May 1974 to 31st March 1978 was Taka 43,800 out of which Taka 28,200 had been paid by defdts. in lump much out of time, that the defdt tenant from 1st May 1974 to 31st March 1978 is required to pay an arrear rent of Taka 15,600 to the plff and that the plff. was entitled to get compensation for unauthorized occupation of the premises by the defdt from 1st April 1978 upto the date of the institution of present suit no 20-3-79 for at least 350 days at the rate of Taka 40 per day amounting to a total of Taka 14,000. The Id SJ decreed the suit in favour of the plff. ordering eviction of the defdt from the suit premises. He also passed a money decree for Taka 29,6000 as arrear rent and compensation against the defdt. Being aggrieved by the said decree the defdt has preferred this appeal. 

 6. Mr M Fazlul Karim, the Id Advocate for the defdt applt. argued that story or oral agreement dated 1-1-75 on the part of the defdt with the plff to pay rent at the rate of Taka 1,000 is not proved, the rent of the premises in question continued to be Taka 600 per month in spite of the written agreement Exhibit 1 dated 1st July 1976 by which defdt agreed to pay rent of Taka 1,000 per month to the plff. with effect from 1st July 1976 as he was not aware of Martial Law Regulation No. II of 1976 date 8-1-76 wherein it was provided that the rent of any premises which was not more than Taka 1,000 per month on the 1st day of December 1975 shall not increased, in view of the acceptance of the rent by the plff. in a lump is should be deemed that the plff. waived the right of ejectment on the ground of default as alleged, that the letters Exhibit 2 and 2(a) dated 22-10-76 were written by the plff. and plff's husband under threat, that as the defdt sent arrear of Taka 11,600 on 10-10-77 by money order and the plff. received the same in lump, it should be deemed that the plff. has waived the right of ejectment of the defdt that since the month of October, 1977 the defdt has been regularly paying rent to the plff. at the rate of Taka 600 by money order upto 31st March 1978, that the rents for the months beginning from 1st April 1978 are deposited in house Rent Control Case No. 20 of 1978 as the plff. refused to accept rent after serving the notice on the defdt u/s 106 of the Transfer of property Act asking him to vacate the premises on 31st March 1977 and that on these grounds the plff's suit should be dismissed and the judgment decree passed by the trial court should be set-aside. 

 7. In this case we have already set out the contents of the documents produced by parties in evidence. PW 1 Hossain Imam Chowdhury, son-in-law of the plff deposed that the plff. purchased the suit premises from the previous owner Mrs Zebunnessa Kabir. His further deposition is as follows. The defdts Used to pay Taka 600 per month as rent to the previous owner. The deft paid rent from May 1974 to December by two instalments at the rate of Taka 600 per month for the second floor. The plff improved and renovated the premises after purchase. It was verbally agreed between the plff and the defdt that the defdt. Will pay rent at the rate of Taka 1,000 per month to the plff for the 2nd floor with effect from 1-1-75. The defdt as DW1 himself proved Exhibit A (5) dated 18-1-75. In this letter he wrote to the Asstt. Controller, Exchange Control Deptt. Bangladesh Bank that he had learnt from an officer of the Cement Factory, Chittagong (who is also tenant of the first floor of the premises in question) that the house in question is probably recorded with the Bangladesh Bank as "Non-resident House". By this letter he wanted to know whether he should pay rent to Mrs Sakina Ahmed (the plff) of the Bangladesh Bank or to the House Rent Controller. The defdt has proved Exhibit A(1) date 1-7-76 by which the Controller of Foreign Exchange, Bangladesh Bank, Dhaka has written to the plaintiff that the plff should pay to Mr Sakina Ahmed monthly rent from May 1974 since she is the owner or the above property and is entitled to receive the rent PW 1 has proved that the defdt, wrote letter Exhibit 2 dated 22-10-76 in his own and under his own signature to the plff's husband which is as follows:— 

 I have already paid taka ten thousand to your son-in-law Mr Hossain Imam being house rent of Surma House, Ctg from July 1976 to September 1976 at the rate of Taka 1,000 per month and Taka 7,000 against outstanding as per letter to your wife. As regards the disputed sum of Taka 1,800. I hope you will not claim for (sic) this amount in view of the slump of my business. I am well. Hope this finds you in good health." 

 "Re : Outstanding Rent of 16, Surma House, Second Floor, 

 A/C of Outstanding Rent 

 There is absolutely no reason to think that these two letters Exhibit 2 and 2(a) clearly show that the rent for the premises in question was agreed between the parties to be Taka 1,000 from 1st January 1975, that the defdt had already defaulted in payment of rent, that the defdt had already defaulted in payment of rent, that he admittedly paid the arrear rents first in a lump of Taka 7000 and that thereafter, he paid the arrear rent of Taka 14000 in two instalments, one instalment by 31-1-77 and another installment by the end of February 1977. Thus this also abundantly shows that the deft is a habitual defaulter PW 1 as state that Exhibit 1 is a written agreement dated 1st July 1976 showing renewal of the lease of the premise in question between the plff and the defdt for payment of rent at the rat of Taka 1000 again from 1st July 1976. In view of the two letters Exhibit 2 and 2(a) which are admittedly in the handwriting of the defendant tenant the lack of reference to the earlier increase of rent to Taka 100 per month with effect from 1-1-75 in Exhibit 1 is of no consequence PW 1 Hossain Imam has truly and correctly stated that the written agreement Exhibit 1 is renewal of monthly lease the rate of rent of which had already fixed at Taka 1000 pm with effect from 1-1-1975. 

 9. DW 1 MM Zaman stated in his deposition that he did not agree to pay the rent of Taka 1000 per month with effect from 1-1-75. The falsity of the statement has been amply established in view of his letters Exhibit 2, Exhibit 2(a) addressed to the plaintiff and plff's husband in his own hand writing. His own money order receipts Exhibit B to Exhibit B(14) show that he paid a total of Taka 11,600 as arrears of rent in lump between 13-10-77 to 18-10-77 in apprehension of the letter from the advocate of the plff Exhibit A(2) dated 19-10-77 asking him to pay the arrear rent and vacate the premises on 31-10-77. This also show clearly that the defdt is a defaulter of the worst kind. The plaint in this letter Exhibit A(2) had claimed as arrear rent of Taka 24,800 as balance up to 30th September 1977. It has been proved from the above discussed evidence that the rent of the premises was fixed at the rate of Taka 1000 with effect from 1-1-75. It has also been proved that plff paid rents on several occasions in lump after being defaulter. The mere fact that the plff accepted the rent does not constitute waiver, acquiescence or estoppels. This view finds sup-port in the case of A Hoque and Co vs Alhaj Zakir Hossain, 1984 BLD (AD) 298 wherein the Appellate Division has observed, "The learned Council for the respondent submitted that it did not require any mentioning as to the non-existence of any express contract varying the requirements as to the payment of rent as laid down in sub-section (5) 18 of the Act. No implied contract either can be said to have been created simply by the fact of payment and acceptance of rents for several months at a time. Such irregular payment did not also constitute a waiver of the right to receive rents as laid down in the aforesaid sub-section. In the absence of any contract as provided in sub-section (5) of section 18 of the Act which, in our opinion, must invariably be a written contract, the date for the payment of rent, as fixed in sub-section (5) of section 18 of the Act is the 15th day of the month next following that for which the rent is payable. As the defdt appellants have not succeeded in proving that there was such a written contract or that rents for the months of May and June were paid within such time as mentioned in the aforesaid sub-section they have become defaulters and cannot escape eviction. Any subsequent deposit of such rents with House Rent Controller cannot enable them to overcome the mischief arising from their default." 

 10. In the case Profulla Kumar Chakraborty vs Anil Proshad Chowdhury, 33 DLR (AD) 55, the Appellate Division had expressed the same view. Undisputedly there was no oral or written contract whatsoever between the parties that the defendant is entitled to pay arrear rents in lump as and when it suits him. In the absence of such contract he has to pay rent for the previous month by the 15th of the following month. As the defendant has not done so as shown above, he is defaulter in the payment of rent on a number of occasions. 

 11. In defendant's own letter Exhibit A (9) dt 10-10-77 he has admitted that even if it is presumed that the rent was not enhanced to Taka 1000 per month from 1-1-75 and that it remained at Taka 600 per month from 1st May, 1974 upto September, 1977, he was still admittedly in arrears in the matter of payment of rent for an amount of Taka 11,600 which he promised to remind soon. Thus, there is no doubt whatsoever that the defendant is a defaulter in the payment of rent. It may be mentioned, however, that we have already shown that it has been clearly proved by the plaintiff by defendant's letters Exhibit 2 and 2 (a) and the evidence of PW 1 that rent of the premises in question was fixed at Taka 1,000 with effect from 1-1-75 by mutual agreement between the parties. 

 12. It is obvious that Martial Law Regulation No. II of 1976 has no application whatsoever in this case as we have found that the rent for the premises in question was mutually fixed between the parties at Taka 1,000 per month with effect from 1st January, 1975. 

 We find that the defendant is a defaulter and therefore, he is not protected from eviction under the Premises Rent Control Ordinance. The defendant is in arrear of rent from 1st May 1974 to 31st March 1978 (as correctly shown in the schedule to the plaint) for an amount of Taka 15,600. The rate of compensation at the rate of Taka 40 per day with effect from 1st April 1978 after the termination of the tenancy is reasonable. Therefore, the compensation for 350 days from 1st April upto the date of institution of the suit on 20-3-79 at the rate of Taka 40 amounting to Taka 14,000 is not in any way excessive. Thus the learned Sub-ordinate Judge has rightly passed money for an amount of Taka 29,600 and has also rightly passed a decree far eviction of the defendant from the premises.
